name: Instruction-following eval v1
description: 104 items whose instructions are checkable by a program: word and character counts, required and forbidden words, casing, bullet and numbered-list shape, paragraph and line structure, opening and closing phrases, exact one-line formats, JSON-only output, answering in a given language with a required keyword, and combinations of the above.
token_heuristic: approx_tokens = ceil(sum(len(m.content) for m in messages) / 4)
provenance: Synthetic, authored in this repository. No third-party text.

answer_extraction: Drop everything inside <think>...</think> (and an unterminated leading <think> block).
Drop markdown code fences, keeping the fenced content.
If any line matches /^\s*(?:final answer|answer)\s*[:\-]\s*(.+)$/i, take the capture of the LAST such line and use only that.
Strip surrounding whitespace, matching quotes, and a single trailing '.' or '!'.
Scorers that need the untouched output (instruction, json) get the raw text as well; the instruction scorer always works on the raw output.

scorers.instruction: Evaluate the rule DSL in `answer` against the RAW output. See eval-instruction-v1/dataset.json for the rule list.

scoring.pass_rule: One item is correct or incorrect; there is no partial credit. accuracy = correct / total. An item whose request failed (timeout, 5xx, context overflow) counts as incorrect AND is reported in scores.failures and metrics.requests_failed.

rule_dsl.shape: answer = {"all": [rule, ...]}; the item is correct only when every rule passes.
rule_dsl.applies_to: the RAW model output — no answer extraction, no trimming. json_only and json_path_equals strip a surrounding markdown fence first.

definitions.word: match of [A-Za-z0-9]+(?:['’-][A-Za-z0-9]+)* — "don't" is one word, "3.5" is two
definitions.paragraph: block from re.split(r'\n\s*\n', text.strip()), empties dropped
definitions.sentence: split on [.!?]+ followed by whitespace or end of text, empties dropped
definitions.bullet: line whose lstrip() starts with a marker followed by a space

rules.word_count: {min?, max?} — number of words is within the range (either bound may be absent)
rules.bullet_count: {min?, max?, markers?=['-','*','•'], only_bullets?=false} — when only_bullets is true every non-empty line must be a bullet
rules.numbered_list: {count} — the numbers found at line starts must be exactly 1..count in order
rules.contains_all: {values[], case_sensitive?=false} — every value occurs as a substring
rules.all_caps: {} — at least one letter, and every cased letter is upper case
rules.all_lower: {} — at least one letter, and every cased letter is lower case
rules.regex: {pattern, flags?='', mode?='search'} — flags is a subset of 'ims'; mode 'fullmatch' matches against text.strip()
rules.not_regex: {pattern, flags?=''} — the pattern must NOT be found anywhere
rules.json_only: {} — the whole output parses as JSON once a surrounding fence is removed
rules.json_path_equals: {path, value} — dotted path (numeric segments index arrays) equals value
rules.is_number: {} — text.strip() with ',' removed parses as a float
rules.word_repeat: {value, min?, max?, case_sensitive?=false} — how often the word occurs
rules.unique_lines: {} — no two non-empty lines are identical after stripping

rule_dsl.reference_implementation: datasets/eval-instruction-v1/rules.py (evaluate(answer, text) -> (bool, failed_rules)); `python datasets/eval-instruction-v1/rules.py --self-test` must pass.

notes: The instruction scorer must evaluate the rule set against the raw output. Stripping <think> blocks first is allowed and recommended for reasoning models; nothing else may be normalised away.
meta.example_pass is a compliant answer written by the generator, used to prove each rule set is satisfiable. It is never sent to the model.
A model that adds a friendly preamble fails most of these items on purpose — that is the capability being measured.
